topics.label: Introduction and lecture overview
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic sets up the lecture by outlining the learning objectives and connecting practical histopathology observations to cellular cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor virology and the discovery of cellular oncogenes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the historical study of transmissible tumor viruses and experimental transformation assays led to the discovery of cellular proto-oncogenes.

topics.label: Classification and genetics of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional criteria and genetic mechanisms distinguishing oncogenes and tumor suppressor mutations using key cell cycle checkpoint paradigms.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the molecular pathways, repair failures, and mitotic defects that give rise to sequence and chromosomal instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the stepwise accumulation of somatic and inherited mutations drives cancer development across familial and sporadic syndromes.

topics.label: Conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the session by reviewing outcomes, inviting student questions, and recommending supplementary reading.
